type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Quick Summary

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **Epic** | #1591 — Epic EQ · Production Deployment Kit (feature group **ENT**) |
| **Level of effort** | M |
| **Effort** | Medium |
| **Priority** | Low |
| **Affected systems** | `scripts` · REST (`ouroboros-rest`) · Docs site (`ouroboros-docs`) |
| **Release** | 🔵 v2 |
| **Milestone** | Enterprise v2 |
| **Type** | Feature |
| **Parallel** | N (after EQ.1, EQ.7) |

Everything a release needs, as files; a list of what calls out

## Design Reference

[`docs/ROADMAP_ENTERPRISE_READINESS.md`](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP_ENTERPRISE_READINESS.md) § Issue EQ.9 is the source of this issue; its *Infrastructure Options* and *Decisions* sections give the reasoning. It was written from the October 2026 competitor gap analysis; facts it marks *unverified* are acceptance criteria here, not assumptions.

## Problem Statement

"Runs with no control plane that holds a copy" is
the product's strongest claim, and its strict form is running with no
outbound network at all. Nobody has listed what Ouroboros calls out to,
so the claim cannot be made for a disconnected network, and there is no
way to carry a release across an air gap.

## Solution / Scope

(1) **Outbound-call inventory:** an audited list of
every destination each service contacts and why (GitHub, configured
model providers, SearXNG's upstreams, the Ollama model registry, the
runner release download, the docs registry, any version check), each
with the variable that disables or redirects it; produced by code review
**and** by running the e2e suite behind a default-deny egress proxy and
recording what was attempted. (2) **Bundle:** `ouroboros-vX.Y.Z-bundle`
— image archives for the manifest's digests, the chart, the compose
files, runner binaries with checksums, the docs-site image, SBOMs and
attestations, and a load-and-retag script for a private registry.
(3) **Offline mode check:** preflight (EQ.2 (#1611)) gains `--offline`, failing
on any configuration that requires an unlisted destination. Local models
through Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on the internal network
are the supported provider path; GitHub Enterprise Server as the source
is **stated as untested** unless tested. Marketplace content is #803's.
Sources: Coder air-gapped install (custom image, chart from releases,
telemetry and update checks disabled, offline licence validation)
[verified]; `HOSTING.md` § 7 (docs site hostable inside a network without
internet access).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The inventory lists every destination observed by the egress proxy
  during the e2e run, with no unexplained entry.
- A stack installed from the bundle on a host with no outbound route
  starts, passes `preflight --offline`, and completes the e2e smoke
  against a local model fixture.
- Bundle contents match the release manifest by digest.
- Anything that does not work offline is listed by name.

## Parallelism / Dependencies

Needs EQ.1 (#1610), EQ.2 (#1611); chart inclusion needs
EQ.7 (#1616); attestations need EQ.8 (#1617). Offline licence validation, if editions
introduce licence keys, belongs to EH–EM. Egress policy for running
agents belongs to DM–DT.

## Technical Stack

`docker save` / `skopeo`, a forward proxy in
default-deny mode for the inventory run, Bash.

## Documentation

Administration — new `deploy/air-gapped.mdx`
(bundle, loading, what is unsupported offline) and
`network-destinations.mdx` (the inventory); CLI `preflight` gains
`--offline`.

## Relationships

- Parent epic: #1591 — Epic EQ · Production Deployment Kit (sub-issue)
- Blocked by: #1610, #1611, #1616, #1617
- Roadmap: [`docs/ROADMAP_ENTERPRISE_READINESS.md`](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP_ENTERPRISE_READINESS.md) · epic EQ · ref `EQ.9`
- Feature code: **ENT** · label `enterprise`

## Diagram

```
connected side                         │ air gap │            disconnected side
release manifest ─▶ bundle.tar ────────┼────────▶│ load-and-retag ─▶ private registry ─▶ compose / helm
  images · chart · runner · docs · SBOM│         │ preflight --offline ─▶ ✓ no unlisted destination
```

items.title: Add debug page to Portal that pings the API (GET /debug/ping)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
  There is currently no way to verify from the Portal itself that it can reach the API. The API already exposes `GET /debug/ping` (returns `pong`), but checking connectivity between Portal and API requires calling the endpoint manually (browser, curl, or the `.http` file). This makes it hard to quickly confirm that routing, proxy configuration and ingress are set up correctly, both locally and after a deployment.
  
  **Describe the solution you'd like**
  Add a debug page to the Portal project (Angular):

  - A new `/debug` route with its own component.
  - A button that sends a `GET` request to the API's `/debug/ping` endpoint.
  - The page shows the result: the response body (`pong`) on success, or a clear error message (status code / network error) on failure.
  - A loading state while the request is in flight.
  - Unit tests for the component and the service that performs the request.

  **Describe alternatives you've considered**
  - Calling `/debug/ping` manually with curl or the `.http` file — works, but does not test the Portal → API path (proxy/ingress) from the browser.
  - Relying on Kubernetes health probes or the Aspire dashboard — these show that the API is up, not that the Portal can reach it.

  **Additional context**
  - The API endpoint already exists in `Sources/MadWorldEU.Meishi.Controllers.Api/Endpoints/DebugEndpoints.cs` and is covered by `DebugEndpointsTests`.
  - The Portal lives in `Sources/MadWorldEU.Meishi.Controllers.Portal`; the dev proxy (`proxy.conf.js`) and the Helm ingress may need to route the debug path to the API.
  - Open question: should the debug page be available in production, or only in development/staging?

items.title: feat(cli): add --summary flag to aicr query for kubectl-style recipe overview
items.body:
## Summary

The output of `aicr query` (and the recipe YAML itself) is very verbose — a typical recipe for a multi-component GPU cluster is hundreds of lines. There is currently no quick way to get a human-readable, at-a-glance overview of what a recipe contains without paging through the full YAML.

## Motivation

Operators running `aicr recipe` or receiving a recipe file need to quickly verify:
- Which cloud service / accelerator / intent the recipe targets
- Which components will be deployed, in what order, and at what versions
- What Kubernetes version and OS constraints apply
- Which validation checks are configured

Today this requires `cat recipe.yaml | grep ...` or manual scrolling. A single flag should surface all of this in seconds.

## Proposed Change

Add two new flags to `aicr query`:

### `--summary`

Prints a concise, `kubectl`-style tabular overview of the recipe. No `--selector` is needed when `--summary` is set.

### `--recipe / -r`

Loads a pre-hydrated `RecipeResult` YAML from disk, bypassing criteria resolution. Mirrors the `--recipe` flag already present on `aicr validate`. When combined with `--selector` it feeds through `client.LoadRecipe`; when combined with `--summary` (and no `--selector`) it uses a fast path that skips `Client` instantiation entirely.

## Example Output

```
$ aicr query --recipe recipe.yaml --summary

RECIPE SUMMARY
============================================================
API Version:     aicr.nvidia.com/v1
Kind:            RecipeResult
Version:         1.0.0
GPU Driver:      pre-installed

CRITERIA
  Service:      eks
  Accelerator:  h100
  Intent:       training
  OS:           ubuntu

OVERLAYS
  Applied:      h100-eks-ubuntu-training

CONSTRAINTS
  K8s.server.version              >= 1.32.4
  Nvidia.driver.version           >= 570.0
  Nvidia.fabricmanager.version    >= 570.0
  Nvidia.cudaToolkit.version      >= 12.8

COMPONENTS (15)
NAME                        TYPE   VERSION    NAMESPACE                  DEPENDS ON
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
network-operator            helm   24.10.0    network-operator           -
gpu-operator                helm   24.9.2     gpu-operator               network-operator
nvidia-device-plugin        helm   0.17.0     nvidia-device-plugin       gpu-operator
dcgm-exporter               helm   3.3.9      dcgm-exporter              gpu-operator
nccl-topology-discovery     helm   0.0.7      nccl-topology-discovery    network-operator
...

VALIDATION
  Deployment:     check-network-operator, check-gpu-operator
  Conformance:    gpu-burn, nccl-all-reduce-bw
  Readiness:      node-feature-discovery
  Performance:    nccl-all-reduce-bw
```

## Implementation Notes

- `--selector` is no longer unconditionally `Required: true`; it is required only when `--summary` is absent (validated manually in the action, so the `urfave/cli` framework does not error before the action runs).
- The summary renderer (`writeRecipeSummary`) writes to `cmd.Root().Writer` so output is testable and redirectable, consistent with the existing CLI output pattern.
- Column widths for the components table are computed dynamically from actual data, with minimum widths initialized from header labels.
- Deployment order comes from `RecipeResult.DeploymentOrder` when populated; falls back to `ComponentRefs` order.

items.title: [Query]  How to ensure only one QueryNode pod is unavailable during Helm upgrades?
items.body:
Hi,

We're running Milvus on Kubernetes using Helm charts and want to ensure QueryNode availability during Helm upgrades.

Since QueryNodes are managed as Kubernetes Deployments, is there a recommended way to ensure that only one QueryNode pod goes down at a time during rolling upgrades?

Specifically:

Does the Helm chart support configuring maxUnavailable: 1 and maxSurge: 1 for QueryNode Deployments?

Are these settings sufficient, or do we need additional configurations such as PodDisruptionBudgets or readiness checks?

How can we ensure that a new QueryNode has loaded its required segments and is ready to serve search traffic before the next pod is terminated?

Is there a recommended approach to achieve zero-downtime QueryNode upgrades using Helm?

Thanks!

items.title: k8s dispatcher and related CI

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
Courier has [dispatchers](https://cira-geoips.github.io/courier/api-reference/dispatchers.html) which can accept `Job` objects with varying `Payloads` (eg. shell, bash, python). The dispatchers are responsible for trying to run the job, emitting dispatcher-specific metrics (general metrics are handled by the base Dispatcher class) and managing the specifics of dispatching as relevant to the dispatcher type.

We do not yet have a dispatcher for k8s or k8s compatible systems. Our goal is to be able to deploy jobs to these systems as [k8s jobs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/) in both parallel and non-parallel fashion. It is currently unclear what a common use case for Parallel Jobs with a fixed completion count would be, so we suggest working on non-parallel and worker-queue parallel jobs first. 

As a part of this work, we also need updates to the testing and CI infrastructure so that we can run full e2e integration tests. This will also set us up well for the eventual goal of being able to specify Courier `Services` as k8s services.

We are assigning this to @jsolbrig to leverage his k8s expertise. Relatedly, @jsolbrig if you believe that the plan of action should be different please comment to that end here to update this your modified plan.

items.title: helm (Go) fails TLS through Cortex proxy on macOS — CA not in System keychain
items.body:
## Summary

Go-based CLI tools (here: `helm`) fail TLS verification when their traffic is routed through the Cortex proxy on macOS, because they do not consult the `*_CA_BUNDLE` / `SSL_CERT_FILE` environment variables Cortex sets, and the Cortex bridge CA is not in the macOS System keychain that Go verifies against.

Filed as a blank issue per the Laptop-feedback template's guidance ("a Helm or platform problem — open a blank issue instead"). Raised with a Cortex maintainer, who suggested filing with details.

## Where it fails

On the **local machine**, not the cluster. A Python CLI shells out to the local `helm` binary, which fetches public Helm chart repos (e.g. `https://llm-d-incubation.github.io/llm-d-infra/`) over the internet via the local Cortex proxy. The cluster API path (`kubectl`/`oc`) is unaffected.

## Symptom

```
helm repo update llmDInfra
Get "https://llm-d-incubation.github.io/llm-d-infra/index.yaml":
  tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

Reproduces both inside the CLI and when `helm repo update` is run standalone in the same shell.

## Works vs. doesn't

- `curl -sSI https://llm-d-incubation.github.io/llm-d-infra/index.yaml` → **HTTP/2 200** (curl honors `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`).
- `helm repo update` → **TLS failure**.

## Root cause (hypothesis)

Cortex sets `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:47600` plus `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `SSL_CERT_FILE` → `~/.cortex/ca/bundle.crt` (valid, 129 certs). curl- and Python-based tools trust the bridge CA via those vars. Go-based tools (helm, and likely `oc`/`kubectl` plugins, `gh` in some builds) do **not** read `*_CA_BUNDLE`, and on macOS Go verifies against the **System keychain** rather than `SSL_CERT_FILE` — where the Cortex CA is absent. So any Go tool doing outbound TLS through the proxy fails.

## Options considered (none applied)

1. Add the Cortex CA to the macOS System keychain (`security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain ~/.cortex/ca/bundle.crt`) — fixes all Go tools, but is a sudo, machine-wide trust change.
2. Bypass the proxy for the helm step (`env -u HTTPS_PROXY ...`) — loses Cortex token visibility for those calls.

## Questions

1. Is adding the bridge CA to the macOS System keychain the intended/supported fix for Go tools, and if so should `install.sh` / `agentop` do it (or offer it)?
2. Is there a supported way for Go/helm to pick up the CA without a system-wide keychain change?
3. Is per-tool proxy bypass acceptable to Cortex's accounting model?

## Environment

- OS: `Darwin arm64`
- Cortex: `agentop v0.8.0`
- `agentop service status`: healthy; TLS bridge CA `~/.cortex/ca/ca.crt` (minted 2026-09-14), env vars point at `~/.cortex/ca/bundle.crt`
- helm: `v4.2.3+g43e8b7f` (Go `go1.25.1 darwin/arm64`)
- Agent: Claude Code, claude-opus-4-8

items.title: externalPostgres: support reading credentials from an existing Secret
items.body:
### Feature request:

#492 added `externalPostgres` for the manager database, but the username and password can only be given as plain values (`externalPostgres.username` / `externalPostgres.password`), which end up in the rendered `manager.yaml` ConfigMap. There is no way to source them from a Kubernetes Secret, e.g. one created by a PostgreSQL operator.

The manager does not read configuration from environment variables (viper's `AutomaticEnv()` is not used), so the usual `env` + `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` route does not work either: the credentials must be present in the YAML file the manager reads.

Proposal (this is what the original #492 branch did before it was trimmed in review):

- `externalPostgres.existingSecret` (+ `usernameKey` / `passwordKey`, defaults `username` / `password`).
- When set, the manager ConfigMap renders placeholders, an init container reads the Secret via `secretKeyRef`, substitutes the placeholders (e.g. `envsubst`) and writes the final `manager.yaml` into an `emptyDir` volume.
- The manager container mounts that `emptyDir` at `/etc/dragonfly` instead of the ConfigMap when `existingSecret` is set.
- Generic building block: `manager.extraInitContainers` (rendered with `common.tplvalues.render`) so operators can plug in their own rendering step.

I am happy to open a PR for this if the approach is acceptable.

### Use case:

Running the manager against a PostgreSQL cluster managed by an operator (Zalando postgres-operator, CloudNativePG, Crunchy, ...). These operators generate the role password and publish it only as a Secret; copying it into Helm values would duplicate a secret into Git and break on rotation. We currently carry this as a local patch on top of the vendored chart.

### UI Example:

```yaml
externalPostgres:
  enable: true
  host: my-postgres
  database: dragonfly_manager
  existingSecret: dragonfly-manager-owner-user.my-postgres.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do
  usernameKey: username
  passwordKey: password
```

items.title: Feature request: move several selected workloads to another host in one reviewed operation
items.body:
**Homestead version:** 2.8.320 · k3s v1.37.1 · 3 nodes (2 workers + a Raspberry Pi tiebreaker)

## Summary

On a node page (Nodes → host → Workloads), the **On this host** card lists the workloads as chips ("9 of yours · 8 system pods") with the hint "Click one to move it to another host", plus **Move everything off**. A user can move one workload at a time, or everything. There is nothing in between: no way to pick 3 of 7 workloads and move just those, to a host of my choosing, as one reviewed operation.

## What I looked for first

I checked the wiki (Containers, Dashboard and nodes, Settings, Storage, Helm and resources), the docs folder (data-move-recovery, design, reference, multi-cluster and others) and all issues, open and closed. I found:

- **Move:** Containers → "Moving between hosts" describes a review for **one** workload. The API matches: `POST /api/move/preview`, then `POST /api/move`, each for one workload with a signed, ten-minute review bound to that workload's destination and resourceVersion.
- **Node level:** Host actions (cordon, drain, reboot) and **Move everything off** act on the whole host.
- **Other bulk actions:** "If a node fails" sets every container in one list, and Containers → ⋯ → **Manage groups** has tick boxes, a filter, **Tick these** and a count that survives filter changes (added via #328). So a tick-and-act pattern already exists, but not for moving.
- **Related issues:** #347 (cluster-wide placement policy, open) asks for a reviewed bulk move back after a node returns; this request is the manual, user-picked version of that. #328 (closed) added the select-all / ticked-count pattern in Manage groups. I found no existing request for selecting several workloads to move.

If this exists and I missed it, a pointer in the docs would be a great outcome too.

## Proposal

1. **Select mode on the "On this host" card.** The chips get tick boxes (or a "Select" toggle that turns them into tick boxes), with a count, "select all" and "clear". Clicking one chip still moves just that one, as today.
2. **Same pattern on the Containers list.** Tick several rows, then **Move selected…**, so I can move workloads between hosts without opening a node page first. Reuse the Manage groups interaction (filter, **Tick these**, ticked count that survives filtering).
3. **One combined review.** Choose a destination host once, with an optional per-workload override. The review lists each workload with its target, downtime (the Recreate strategy), capacity fit on the destination *including the other selected workloads*, and its warnings. Blocked workloads are marked and can be unticked, not fail the whole batch. Examples are workloads pinned for hardware, host-local storage, a direct `nodeName`, spread rules, or a paused workload.
4. **Safe execution.** Run the moves one at a time, or in small batches. Honour PodDisruptionBudgets, stop on the first failure, and show progress in **Recent jobs** with a per-workload result. The signed review would cover the whole set, so a concurrent edit to any one workload conflicts instead of being overwritten.
5. **"Move everything off" becomes "select all".** It would open the same combined review, so the two paths share the safety checks.

## Why

- Real maintenance is rarely all or nothing. Before a reboot I may want to move only the CI/build workloads off a host, or after a node returns, put back a few apps that belong there. Today that is a review per workload, repeated.
- Per-workload reviews cannot see each other. Moving three workloads one by one means each review checks capacity as if the others were not coming, so the combined review gives a more honest capacity check.
- It reuses what Homestead already has: the move review, the tick-and-count pattern from Manage groups, and Recent jobs.

## Context

Today, after a RAM upgrade, k3s-02 shows seven workloads on the card: arc-controller, buildkitd, cloudflared, k3s-dipsentry, k3s-homelab-scripts, mcp-smoke and n8n-mcp. A typical case is moving two or three of them, for example the apps that belong on the other host after a failover, while leaving the rest alone. "Move everything off" is too much for that, and three separate reviews are slow and can't see each other's capacity. (Some of these are pinned to the host by their own manifests; the combined review marking those as blocked, rather than failing the batch, is exactly what point 3 asks for.)

Related: #347 (placement policy and rebalancing after recovery), #328 (select-all pattern in Manage groups).

items.title: Every {{...}} in a task is a cigo template, so go list -f, docker --format and gh --template cannot be passed through
items.body:
## What happens

`cigo` reads every `{{...}}` in a task's `cmd`, `shell`, `env`, `stdin`, `cwd` and `undo_shell` as one of its own templates (`{{task}}`, `{{task.field}}`, `{{env.NAME}}`, `{{root}}`, `{{x|json}}`, `{{x|sh}}`). There is no way to write a literal `{{` for the program the task runs. Go's `-f`, Docker's `--format`, `gh --template`, goreleaser and Helm all take `{{...}}` templates of their own, so a task that calls one of them cannot be written.

Where: `orchestrate.cig:1814` (`TEMPLATE = '\{\{[^{}]*\}\}'`), `render` at `orchestrate.cig:1936-1955` (every match is replaced or refused) and the check at `orchestrate.cig:3351` ("names no task").

## To reproduce

```sh
mkdir probe && cd probe
printf '%s\n' '{"project": "probe", "tasks": {"pkgs": {"cmd": ["go", "list", "-f", "{{.ImportPath}}", "./..."], "capture": "lines"}}}' > cig-tasks.json
cigo check; echo "exit=$?"
cigo run pkgs; echo "exit=$?"
```

cig-orchestrator 0.2.0 on cig 1.1.1, 2026-10-09:

```
cig-tasks.json: 1 task(s), 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)
  error: pkgs: {{.ImportPath}} names no task; tasks here: pkgs
exit=1
probe: pkgs

stopped at pkgs; cig puts back what this run changed, newest first
Don't see any cigarettes.
error[E600 cough]: {{.ImportPath}} in task `pkgs`: no task by that name has produced output in this run; give it `capture`, or have it write name=value lines to $CIG_OUTPUT
  --> /home/jay/.local/share/cig-orchestrator/orchestrate.cig:2585:5
```

## What should happen

A manifest must be able to hand `{{.ImportPath}}` to `go list` untouched. Two changes, and both together would be best:

1. **An escape.** `{{{{` and `}}}}` render as literal braces, so one argument can mix a cigo value with a Go template: `["docker", "ps", "--format", "{{{{.ID}}}} {{project}}"]`. The regex at 1814 and `render` need to skip a four-brace run and emit two braces.
2. **A switch per task.** `"templates": false` on a task turns rendering off for every string of that task, so a command copied from a tool's documentation works as pasted. When `cigo check` meets a `{{...}}` that names no task, its message should mention the switch: "not a task of this manifest; if it is the program's own template, set \"templates\": false on the task".

`docs/manifest.md` (the Templates section at line 140) should then list the programs whose arguments collide (`go list -f`, `go test -run` does not, `docker --format`, `gh --template`, goreleaser, Helm) and the escape.

## Why it matters

Found while adopting cig-orchestrator for a Go project whose checks include `go list -f '{{.ImportPath}}' ./...` and whose release step formats `gh` output. Both had to move into shell files, which is the glue the tool exists to remove. The workaround that works today, for anyone who hits this first: put the command in a script file and run the file.

items.title: Audit: workloads still on the archived k8s-at-home project (dead images + frozen 2022 charts)
items.body:
Audited (2026-10-09) every workload still backed by the archived **k8s-at-home** project — charts from
`https://k8s-at-home.com/charts/` and images under `ghcr.io/k8s-at-home/*`. The project was archived
**2022-08-21**; its chart index still returns HTTP 200 but is frozen at `generated: 2022-08-19`.

Full working report (long form, with per-release table and verification notes):
`scratchpad/k8s-at-home-audit.md` (local, not committed).

## Headline

**21** HelmRelease files use the `k8s-at-home` HelmRepository; **20** are deployed, **1** (`rtorrent`) is orphaned.

The expectation going in was "these images are pinned as chart defaults, so renovate can't see them."
**That is mostly false** — 18 of the 20 deployed releases set `image.repository` + `image.tag` in the
HelmRelease `values:`, and Dependency Dashboard #3 confirms detection for all of them. Most already run
maintained images (LSIO arr apps, official home-assistant / esphome / frigate / jellyfin / tvheadend,
byparr, jacobalberty/unifi).

Two real problems remain:

1. **A small number of genuinely dead images, and the invisible ones are the worst of them.**
2. **The charts themselves** — all 20 are 2022 artefacts with no upstream successor.

## Dead `ghcr.io/k8s-at-home/*` images running right now (4 distinct, 6 workloads)

Build dates verified by GHCR manifest → config-blob walk.

| Image | Built | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pod-gateway:v1.5.0` | 2022-04-30 | `network/vpn-gateway` (main+init), **injected** into `vpn/transmission` and `vpn/qbittorrent` | repo max is `v1.7.0` (2022-08-14) |
| `gateway-admision-controller:v3.3.2` | **2021-06-07** | `network/vpn-gateway-pod-gateway-webhook` | chart default, invisible to renovate |
| `cni-plugins:v1.1.1` | 2022-06-20 | `network-system/multus` init container | CNI on all 6 nodes |
| `intel-gpu-plugin:v0.22.0` | **2021-10-01** | `util-system/intel-gpu-plugin` | upstream `intel/intel-gpu-plugin` is at **0.37.1**; the chart's own default was already the upstream image, so our override is pointless |

## The 3 images renovate genuinely cannot see

All three come from chart-default values (the bundled `common` 4.3.0/4.5.2 library), not from anything in this repo:

| Release | Container | Image | Built |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network/vpn-gateway` | `webhook` | `ghcr.io/k8s-at-home/gateway-admision-controller:v3.3.2` | 2021-06-07 |
| `network/vpn-gateway` | `openvpn` | `dperson/openvpn-client:latest` | **2021-03-31** — carries all VPN egress |
| `vpn/transmission` | `netshoot` | `ghcr.io/nicolaka/netshoot:v0.7` | 2022 era (qbittorrent already pins v0.16 in-repo) |

(`media/tvheadend` is also renovate-invisible, but deliberately: `tag: latest` + `pullPolicy: Always` +
the 2am `daily-restart.yaml` is the update mechanism. `rtorrent` has no image key and isn't deployed.)

## 5 chart versions invisible to renovate

`tvheadend`, `sonarr`, `radarr`, `prowlarr`, `lidarr`.

The chart-version custom manager in `.github/renovate.json5` requires a `# renovate: registryUrl=…`
comment **and** `version:` on the line immediately after `chart:`. The four arr releases have no comment
at all and put `version:` after the `sourceRef:` block; tvheadend has the comment but the same ordering
problem. Confirmed against the `regex (64)` section of Dependency Dashboard #3 — none of the five appear.

Worth noting this unlocks only 2022 charts (`sonarr`/`radarr` 15.x → 16.3.2, `tvheadend` 5.0.1 → 5.4.2,
`pod-gateway` 5.3.0 → 5.6.2), so it is hygiene rather than value.

## Migration target and its ceiling

bjw-s **`app-template` 3.7.3** (`kubeVersion >=1.22.0-0`). **4.0.0 through 5.2.1 all declare `>=1.28.0-0`**
and will not install on 1.24 — renovate PR #3024 (app-template v5) must stay closed until the cluster
climb reaches 1.28 (#2843). Strong in-repo precedent already on 3.7.3: `sabnzbd`, `ombi`, `seerr`, `epg`,
`qbittorrent`, `netbootxyz`, `ninerouter`, `emhass`, `evcc-optimizer`.

## Work, in the order it is worth doing

### Tier 0 — free deletions
- [ ] Delete `cluster/apps/downloads/rtorrent/` — absent from `cluster/apps/downloads/kustomization.yaml` and from the cluster.
- [ ] Drop `ghcr.io/k8s-at-home/radarr` and `ghcr.io/k8s-at-home/sonarr` from the automerge `packageRules` in `.github/renovate.json5` — both arrs run LSIO images now, so those matchers are dead config.
- [ ] Remove the stale pod-gateway values-file comment at `cluster/apps/network/unifi/helmrelease.yaml:21`.

### Tier 1 — image overrides only, no chart change
- [ ] `intel-gpu-plugin`: `ghcr.io/k8s-at-home/intel-gpu-plugin:v0.22.0` → `intel/intel-gpu-plugin:0.37.1`. Jellyfin's `gpu.intel.com/i915` request depends on this DaemonSet; whether 0.37.x still supports k8s 1.24 is **unverified** — step through 0.2x/0.3x if it balks.
- [ ] `transmission`: pin `addons.netshoot.image` to `ghcr.io/nicolaka/netshoot:v0.16` (copy qbittorrent). Trivial — debug sidecar only.
- [ ] `vpn-gateway`: pin `webhook.image` explicitly (max available `v3.6.0`) — **stopgap only**, the image is still dead. Skip if #2852 lands soon.
- [ ] `mosquitto` `2.0.22` → `2.1.2` (check 2.1 config deltas).
- [ ] `node-red` `3.1.15` → `5.0.8` (#2731) — two majors; `flows.json` and custom nodes live only on the PVC, snapshot first.
- [ ] `jellyfin` `10.11.11` → `12.2` — major line jump, in-place config migration **unverified**.
- [ ] Renovate hygiene: add the `# renovate:` comment and move `version:` directly under `chart:` for tvheadend/sonarr/radarr/prowlarr/lidarr.

### Tier 2 — chart migration to app-template 3.7.3 (mechanical, PVC carry-over via `existingClaim`)
Easiest → hardest: `flaresolverr` (stateless — ideal pilot) → `jackett`/`prowlarr`/`sonarr`/`radarr`/`lidarr`
(config PVC + NFS mounts + `supplementalGroups: 816` + PUID/PGID; `lidarr`'s `DOCKER_MODS` env must keep its
exact `name:tag` shape or that renovate manager stops matching) → `mosquitto`/`appdaemon`/`esphome`
(the latter two need the `codeserver` addon hand-rolled as a second container — app-template 3.x has no `addons`)
→ `node-red` → `transmission` (the `setGateway: "true"` annotation must survive verbatim or the pod leaks
outside the VPN) → `jellyfin` (many `type: custom` NFS volumes, Intel GPU, NFS transcode cache) →
`tvheadend` (DVB node selector, `privileged`, `supplementalGroups: [44]`, the configMap-mounted
`tv_grab_url` at mode 0755 — app-template 3.x handles this natively, which is an improvement).

### Tier 3 — risky / stateful, one PR each
- [ ] **`vpn-gateway` → `angelnu/pod-gateway` 7.1.1 — highest priority, already drafted in #2852.** Kills three dead images at once and removes the injected dead sidecars from both `transmission` and `qbittorrent`. Needs the SOPS secret, the `routed-gateway` namespace label, and a live egress leak test (killing `openvpn` must block, not leak).
- [ ] **`multus`** — CNI on all 6 nodes; the macvlan NADs for `home-assistant`, `home-assistant-dad` and `frigate` ride on it. **Reconcile the live drift first (see the separate issue).** Target `bjw-s-labs/multus` 1.3.5 (appVersion 4.2.4), which drops the `cni-plugins` init container entirely — but `cni.netPath`/`cni.binPath` must be overridden to the k3s paths (`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/cni/net.d`, `/var/lib/rancher/k3s/data/current/bin`).
- [ ] **`home-assistant` + `home-assistant-dad`** — biggest blast radius: macvlan static-IP annotations, three `additionalContainers` (codeserver, nginx, zigbee-flush with an inline script in a chart-generated `configmap:` block — no app-template equivalent, these become real manifests), two `subPath` mounts with `mountPath: "-"`, and a `/config` PVC whose contents are not in git. Do `-dad` first as the rehearsal.
- [x] **`frigate`** — `privileged`, `/dev/usb` hostPath for the Coral TPU, NFD-label node affinity, and a `webrtc` LoadBalancer exposing TCP+UDP on the same port 8555. Hardware passthrough + dual-protocol LB is the risk, not the chart.

### Adjacent debt (not k8s-at-home, same shape)
7 releases are on bjw-s `app-template` **0.2.2**, which predates the `controllers` API — a separate, smaller
rewrite to 3.7.3: `evcc`, `signtools`, `tesla-proxy`, `teslamate`, `teslamate-abrp` (currently `Ready=False`),
`teslamate-grafana`, `network/uisp`.

## Not verified
Intel GPU plugin 0.37.x on k8s 1.24 · Jellyfin 10→12 in-place config migration · `bjw-s-labs/multus` 1.3.5
on 1.24 (declares no `kubeVersion`, which is absence of a constraint, not evidence of support) · whether every
`type: custom` NFS volume maps 1:1 onto app-template `persistence` (no `helm template` run for any proposed
migration) · why renovate offers no jellyfin 12.x and no mosquitto 2.1.x despite both existing upstream.

items.title: [BUG]Provisioning v2 (Harvester node driver): Machine.status.addresses is not refreshed after a DHCP change, so new nodes get a stale server: join address

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Issues that are defects reported by users or that we know have reached a real release

items.body:
**Rancher Server Setup**
- Rancher version: `v2.13.3`
- Installation option (Docker install/Helm Chart): Helm Chart (`rancher-2.13.3`)
   - If Helm Chart, Kubernetes Cluster and version (RKE1, RKE2, k3s, EKS, etc): k3s `v1.34.6+k3s1`
- Proxy/Cert Details: none

**Information about the Cluster**
- Kubernetes version: `v1.34.9+rke2r1`
- Cluster Type (Local/Downstream): Downstream
   - If downstream, what type of cluster? (Custom/Imported or specify provider for Hosted/Infrastructure Provider): Infrastructure Provider, Harvester node driver (`docker-machine-driver-harvester` `v1.0.4`). Harvester `1.8.2`; 3 control plane nodes (control-plane, etcd) and 3 workers on Ubuntu 24.04, all on DHCP without reservations.

**User Information**
- What is the role of the user logged in? (Admin/Cluster Owner/Cluster Member/Project Owner/Project Member/Custom): Admin
  - If custom, define the set of permissions: not applicable

**Describe the bug**

After a Harvester upgrade restarted every VM, two of the three control plane VMs received new DHCP addresses. etcd kept the old peer URLs, and I corrected them with `etcdctl member update`. The cluster is healthy again. The Rancher `Machine` objects still hold the old addresses, so every new node is given the former address of one control plane node as its join target.

I scaled a worker pool up by 1. `rancher-system-agent` wrote this to `/etc/rancher/rke2/config.yaml.d/50-rancher.yaml` on the new node:

```
"server": "https://10.20.0.147:9345",
```

`10.20.0.147` is the former address of control plane node `cp-b`. Its live address is `10.20.0.87`. The new node cannot reach the old address:

```
$ nc -vz -w 5 10.20.0.147 9345
nc: connect to 10.20.0.147 port 9345 (tcp) failed: No route to host
```

`rke2-agent` loops on:

```
Failed to validate connection to cluster at https://10.20.0.147:9345: failed to get CA certs: Get "https://127.0.0.1:6444/cacerts": read tcp 127.0.0.1:41550->127.0.0.1:6444: read: connection reset by peer
```

The `Machine` stays in `Provisioning`, with no `NODENAME` or `PROVIDERID`, indefinitely.

**To Reproduce**

1. Provision a Harvester node driver cluster with control plane nodes on DHCP without reservations.
2. Shut down the control plane VMs and start them again, so that at least one receives a different address.
3. Repair the cluster itself, for example the etcd peer URL of that member.
4. Scale a machine pool up by 1.
5. Read `/etc/rancher/rke2/config.yaml.d/50-rancher.yaml` on the new node.

**Result**

`server:` holds the control plane node's address from before the DHCP change. The new node never joins.

The `Machine` objects in `fleet-default` still report the pre change addresses:

```
$ kubectl -n fleet-default get machines.cluster.x-k8s.io downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpb -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses}'
[{"address":"10.20.0.147","type":"InternalIP"},{"address":"downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpb","type":"Hostname"}]

$ kubectl -n fleet-default get machines.cluster.x-k8s.io downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpa -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses}'
[{"address":"10.20.0.111","type":"InternalIP"},{"address":"downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpa","type":"Hostname"}]
```

`kubectl get nodes -o wide` in the downstream cluster shows the live addresses, `10.20.0.87` for `cp-b` and `10.20.0.107` for `cp-a`. The former address of `cp-a`, `10.20.0.111`, is now assigned to a worker. No `Machine` in the cluster is stuck in `Deleting` or `Failed`.

The stale value is already present on the `HarvesterMachine` objects (`harvestermachines.rke-machine.cattle.io`), while Harvester itself reports the live addresses:

```
$ kubectl -n fleet-default get harvestermachines.rke-machine.cattle.io downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpb -o yaml
  status:
    addresses:
    - address: 10.20.0.147
      type: InternalIP
    - address: downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpb
      type: Hostname
    ready: true

$ kubectl -n fleet-default get harvestermachines.rke-machine.cattle.io downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpa -o yaml
  status:
    addresses:
    - address: 10.20.0.111
      type: InternalIP
    - address: downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpa
      type: Hostname
    ready: true
```

```
$ kubectl get vmi -A -o wide   (Harvester cluster)
NAMESPACE    NAME                                 PHASE     IP           NODENAME           READY
downstream   downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpc   Running   10.20.0.112  harvester-node-2   True
downstream   downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpa   Running   10.20.0.107  harvester-node-5   True
downstream   downstream-control-plane-abcde-cpb   Running   10.20.0.87   harvester-node-3   True
```

`cp-c` kept its original address (`10.20.0.112`) after the restart, so only `cp-a` and `cp-b` are affected. I did not inspect the `cp-c` `HarvesterMachine`.

**Expected Result**

The join address reflects the node's current address, or `Machine.status.addresses` is refreshed when the address changes.

**Screenshots**

Not applicable.

**Additional context**

- The stale value is on the `HarvesterMachine` object for both affected nodes, and Harvester reports the correct address for both. It appears that `Machine.status.addresses` copies the `HarvesterMachine` value, and that `server:` in `50-rancher.yaml` is built from it, because the value in `50-rancher.yaml` matches the `Machine` record exactly. I have not confirmed which controller sets this field or whether anything refreshes it after the first provisioning.
- Both `HarvesterMachine` objects record `networkInfo` with `"macAddress":""` for the interface `default/vmnet-untagged`. I do not know whether that matters.
- RKE2 documentation says server addresses should be static, and I am adding DHCP reservations. This issue is about Rancher not noticing an address change on a node that is otherwise healthy, which blocks every later node join.
- Related: harvester/harvester#2099 (a new node tried to join an address that DHCP had since assigned to a different machine).
- I have not edited any Rancher object.

Questions:

1. Which controller sets `HarvesterMachine.status.addresses`, and should it refresh the value after the VM's address changes?
2. Is there a supported way to correct a stale address, such as patching `HarvesterMachine.status.addresses`? I would rather not patch `status` on a live control plane without confirmation.
3. If I replace the affected control plane nodes through Rancher by adding one node and deleting the old one, will the new node pick another stale address as its join target?

items.title: [Bug]: Woodpecker WAL truncation stops on 4 pchannels; Completed segment without footer.blk freezes consume checkpoint, segment metadata grows in etcd without limit (v2.6.5 / woodpecker v0.1.6)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Issues or changes related a bug

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Environment

```markdown
- Milvus version: v2.6.5 (Helm chart milvus-5.0.7, installed 2025-11-10, never upgraded)
- Deployment mode(standalone or cluster): cluster, streaming service enabled (mixcoord, streamingnode, querynode, datanode, proxy)
- MQ type(rocksmq, pulsar or kafka): woodpecker v0.1.6 (embedded), storage type minio, metadata in etcd (prefix woodpecker)
- SDK version(e.g. pymilvus v2.0.0rc2): not relevant; the problem is server-side and occurs without client action
- OS(Ubuntu or CentOS): Ubuntu 22.04 (kernels 5.15 and 6.5), Kubernetes RKE2 v1.24.12, containerd 1.6.19
- CPU/Memory: Milvus nodes 48 cores / 378 GiB; etcd nodes 24 cores / 126 GiB; no resource requests or limits on Milvus or etcd pods
- GPU: none
- Others:
etcd: milvusdb/etcd:3.5.18-r1, 3 members, PVCs on Ceph RBD (HDD-backed pool), DB about 1 GB of a 4 GB quota
MinIO: minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-12-18T13-15-44Z, 4 pods, distributed, on Ceph
16 pchannels, 1 collection (on dml_0)
Changed from default: streaming.walBalancer.operationTimeout: 30m (since 2026-07-29; 2.6.5 default is 30s)
All woodpecker.* and streaming.walTruncate.* values are defaults (sampleInterval 30m, retentionInterval 72h, auditor.maxInterval 10s, segmentRollingPolicy.maxInterval 10m)
```

### Current Behavior

Current Behavior
On 4 of 16 pchannels (`by-dev-rootcoord-dml_1`, `_5`, `_6`, `_15`), the StreamingNode consume checkpoint has not moved for 93 to 194 days. Woodpecker never truncates these channels, and their segment metadata in etcd grows by one key for each new segment. etcd now holds 345,002 keys; 342,033 of them are woodpecker segment keys of these 4 channels.

**Segment keys per log** (`etcdctl get woodpecker/ --prefix --keys-only`, grouped):

| channel | 2026-07-29 | 2026-08-12 | 2026-10-08 |
|---|---|---|---|
| dml_5 | ~134,827 | 135,528 | 138,188 |
| dml_6 | ~134,757 | 135,509 | 138,172 |
| dml_15 | ~38,476 | 39,180 | 41,851 |
| dml_1 | ~20,453 | 21,158 | 23,822 |
| each of the other 12 | | | 231–259, stable |

**Consume checkpoint** (`by-dev/meta/streamingnode-meta/wal/<pchannel>/consume-checkpoint`, decoded; etcd revision at read time 12,042,976):

| channel | segment | checkpoint time (UTC) | mod_revision |
|---|---|---|---|
| dml_5 | 49 | 2026-03-28 14:08 | 4,162,329 |
| dml_6 | 51 | 2026-03-28 14:09 | 4,162,425 |
| dml_15 | 465 | 2026-06-22 19:13 | 7,893,438 |
| dml_1 | 691 | 2026-07-07 05:28 | 8,661,143 |
| dml_9 (healthy) | 1221 (current) | seconds ago | current |

The last truncation in `woodpecker/logs/<pchannel>` is from the same period: dml_5 2026-03-27 (segment 40), dml_6 2026-03-27 (39), dml_15 2026-06-18 (463), dml_1 2026-06-27 (508).

**One old Completed segment without a footer on each stuck channel.** The auditor reports it every 10 s as `segment must be finalized before compaction`:

| channel (logId) | segment | created (UTC) | etcd segment meta | objects under `<bucket>/file/wp/<logId>/<segId>/` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dml_5 (6) | 24787 | 2026-04-15 02:00 | state=Completed, lastEntryId=0, size 77, version 2 | `0.blk` 148B, `m_0.blk` 148B, `write.lock` 97B |
| dml_6 (2) | 53195 | 2026-05-18 06:12 | same | same 3 objects |
| dml_15 (16) | 14829 | 2026-07-04 20:40 | same | same 3 objects |
| dml_1 (14) | 9131 | 2026-07-17 03:24 | same | same 3 objects |

There is no `footer.blk` and no fence block. A healthy segment (dml_9 segment 1220) has metadata state 3, lastEntryId 1, version 3, and objects `2.blk` (1B fence), `footer.blk` (86B), `m_0.blk`, `write.lock`.

**Effect.** The auditor lists all segments of each log every 10 s: 3.5 s per cycle for dml_5, about 0.1 s for a healthy channel. The large range reads (2–4 MB on 2026-08-02, 14 MB on 2026-08-12) slow etcd: in 30 minutes, 908 / 2,910 / 2,940 `apply request took too long` warnings on the 3 members. Then every Milvus component loses its etcd lease and exits (`session key is deleted, exit...`, `requested lease not found`). Restart counts: proxy 2,144, mixcoord 1,554, querynode 1,587, streamingnode 1,656, datanode 3,397.

Clean in the same 30 minutes: `segment storage not writable`, `failed to recover from wal`, `EntryNotFound`, `context deadline exceeded`, `fail to assign channel`, `etcdserver: request is too large`. In the same window we found no `pendingReadSegmentId` reader lines for any channel.

### Expected Behavior

Expected Behavior
- The consume checkpoint of every pchannel advances, and `streaming.walTruncate` truncates the WAL after `retentionInterval` (72h).
- The woodpecker auditor finalizes, fences or skips a `Completed` segment that has no `footer.blk`, so truncation does not stop on it.
- Woodpecker segment metadata in etcd stays bounded, as it does on the 12 healthy channels (about 230 keys each).
- After an object-storage write failure, Milvus recovers by itself, without manual repair of WAL objects.

### Steps To Reproduce

```markdown
We have no deterministic reproduction. The sequence we observed:

1. Run a Milvus v2.6.5 cluster with streaming and woodpecker v0.1.6 on MinIO, with MinIO on Ceph-backed storage.
2. MinIO becomes unwritable for a period (we saw `Sync failed: segment storage not writable` in a July incident, and repeated MinIO drive offline events from December to April).
3. A segment on a channel reaches state `Completed`. Compaction writes `m_0.blk`, but `footer.blk` is never written.
4. The consume checkpoint of that channel stops advancing. WAL truncation stops. A new segment key is added in etcd every rolling interval and is never removed.
5. The auditor lists the growing segment set every 10 s. etcd slows down, components lose their leases and restart, and each restart replays recovery from the old checkpoint.

In July we repaired 7 segments with the same layout (no footer) by hand (see "Anything else?"). The 4 segments above were not detected at that time.
```

### Milvus Log

 Milvus Log
StreamingNode, repeated every 10 s (2026-10-08):

```
[WARN] [segment/segment_handle.go:1045] ["Segment compaction operation failed"] [logName=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_5,logId=6,segmentId=24787 [error="segment must be finalized before compaction"]] [stack="github.com/zilliztech/woodpecker/woodpecker/segment.(*segmentHandleImpl).Compact\n\t/go/pkg/mod/github.com/zilliztech/woodpecker@v0.1.6/woodpecker/segment/segment_handle.go"]
[INFO] [segment/segment_handle.go:984] ["Validating segment state for compaction"] [logName=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_5,logId=6,segmentId=24787,currentState=Completed,currentLastEntryId=0,currentSize=0]
[WARN] [log/internal_log_writer.go:278] ["auditor maintain the log segment failed"] [logName=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_5,logId=6,segId=24787 [error="segment must be finalized before compaction"]]
[INFO] [log/internal_log_writer.go:297] ["Auditor segment processing completed"] [logName=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_5,logId=6,segmentsProcessed=2,segmentsCompacted=0,segmentsFailed=2,truncatedSegments=0]
[INFO] [log/internal_log_writer.go:312] ["Auditor cycle completed"] [logName=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_5,logId=6,duration=3.547284392s,totalSegments=138188,truncatedSegments=0]
```

Healthy channel for comparison:

```
[INFO] [log/internal_log_writer.go:312] ["Auditor cycle completed"] [logName=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_14,logId=10,duration=142.425648ms,totalSegments=233,truncatedSegments=0]
```

Proxy, at the last crash (2026-10-08 17:11 UTC):

```
[INFO] [sessionutil/session_util.go:974] ["session key is deleted, exit..."] [role=proxy]
[WARN] [sessionutil/session_util.go:609] ["fail to retry keepAliveOnce"] [serverName=proxy] [error="etcdserver: requested lease not found"]
[ERROR] [proxy/proxy.go:163] ["Proxy disconnected from etcd, process will exit"]
```

Full logs from the export-log script are available on request.

### Anything else?

Anything else?
**History**

- 2026-04-07 and 2026-04-20: `streamingcoord-meta/pchannel/dml_5` and `dml_6` grew to about 767 KB each from appended historical assignment records. MixCoord failed with `etcdserver: request is too large`, and queries failed with `Timestamp lag too large`. Workaround both times: back up and delete `by-dev/meta/streamingcoord-meta/pchannel/`, restart MixCoord (and StreamingNode/QueryNode if timestamps stayed frozen).
- 2026-07-29: after MinIO became unwritable, 7 segments had state `Completed` without `footer.blk`. Their readers read entry 0, asked for entry 1, got `EntryNotFound` and retried forever. The 30 s `walBalancer.operationTimeout` cancelled recovery; we raised it to 30m. We repaired the 7 segments (dml_0 1116 and 1121, dml_1 694, dml_2 868, dml_5 62, dml_6 53, dml_15 466) with woodpecker v0.1.6's own `FenceSegment` logic. It wrote only a 1-byte fence `1.blk` and `footer.blk`, and changed no existing object or etcd key. dml_0 and dml_2 recovered and truncate normally since then.
- We have not deleted any `woodpecker/` key, reset any checkpoint, or upgraded Milvus.

**Questions**

1. Is a Completed segment without `footer.blk` the reason why the consume checkpoint is frozen on these 4 channels? If not, what is?
2. What is the supported way to finalize or fence these segments? Is the `FenceSegment` method from July safe for them?
3. Why does woodpecker v0.1.6 leave a Completed segment without a footer, and why does the auditor not fence it itself? Is this fixed in a later woodpecker version?
4. After the checkpoint advances, will `walTruncate` and the auditor remove the backlog of about 342,000 segment keys by themselves? How long will it take, and how much etcd write load will it cause?
5. Is there a supported way to discard WAL history on a pchannel that holds no vchannel? None of dml_1/5/6/15 holds one now.
6. Which 2.6.x release and woodpecker version do you recommend? Which fixes apply to: the missing footer after a storage write failure, stopped truncation, accumulating pchannel assignment history, and the 30s `walBalancer.operationTimeout` default?
7. Is deleting `streamingcoord-meta/pchannel/` plus a MixCoord restart a supported recovery? Can it lose state or make the woodpecker backlog worse?
8. Can we upgrade safely while the backlog exists, or must we fix it first?
9. Can the auditor avoid listing every segment key every 10 s?
10. Is HDD-backed network block storage supported for the Milvus etcd?

**Possibly related issues**

-  woodpecker truncation races segment completion (fixed in woodpecker v0.1.40, 3.0 branch)
-  channel checkpoint lag growth and etcd OOM (v2.6.1)
-  streaming nodes crash-loop on a stale checkpoint and WAL replay
-  orphaned segment-assign meta is never removed from etcd (2.6)

This is a production cluster. We will not change etcd or object-storage data without a procedure that the Milvus team approves. We can provide decoded etcd values, object listings and the content of the 4 segments, configuration, and full logs.

items.title: A consistent way to pass each site's service settings to the API and PWA
items.body:
Split out of #123. A loose idea to work through, not a proposal.

## The problem

Each site builds different services in, such as maps, analytics, consent, bot protection, spreadsheets or sign-in providers, and each needs its own settings on the **front end, the API, or both**. The template has no consistent way to get those settings from CI into the API and PWA containers, so every project wires them up its own way. That makes projects harder to compare with the template and with each other, and every new service means designing the plumbing again.

## How projects do it today

- **Cymru Kitchens:** Google Maps, Meta Pixel and Tag Manager as Docker build args baked into the app image, plus a Kubernetes Secret read by the PWA. A change needs a rebuild.
- **HBCP and SRNT-E:** Tag Manager (and SRNT-E's Maps key) in the ConfigMap, filled from CI variables, with Tag Manager blanked on staging and review apps so test traffic isn't counted as the live site's.
- **smoking-and-alcohol-websites:** a `site:` block of Helm values (country, topic, name, Tag Manager, Turnstile) and `php.google`/`php.turnstile` values, passed to both the API and the PWA, with secrets in the Secret.

## Questions to resolve

- Is there a consistent way to map a project's own variables through `k8s.sh` and the chart to the API, the PWA, or both, without editing `k8s.sh`, `values.yaml` and several chart templates for every new one?
- Public values (ConfigMap) and secret ones (Secret): how does a project say which is which?
- Build time (baked into the image) or runtime (container environment): when is each needed?
- Values that depend on the deploy track, like analytics blanked outside production: where does that logic live?
- Environment variables are likely to stay the mechanism, at least for some of this, but that's an open question too. Some settings might suit configuration managed elsewhere. It needs much more thought.

labels.description: Docs and issues related to Camunda Platform 8 Self-Managed

items.body:
## Problem

The Operate configuration property `camunda.operate.tasklist-url` (env `CAMUNDA_OPERATE_TASKLISTURL`) is not documented anywhere, on any version of the docs.

It is a real, user-facing property: it is what makes Operate render the "Open Tasklist" deep link on a user task in the process instance **Details** tab. When it is unset — which is the default — the link is silently omitted, with no error and no hint in the UI that configuration is missing. Without documentation there is no way for a Self-Managed operator to discover that the feature exists, let alone that it needs configuring.

This surfaced while investigating [camunda/camunda#65161](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/issues/65161), where the missing link took a source-level investigation to explain precisely because the property is undocumented.

## What I checked

- [`docs/self-managed/components/orchestration-cluster/operate/operate-configuration.md`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda-docs/blob/main/docs/self-managed/components/orchestration-cluster/operate/operate-configuration.md) — no occurrence of `tasklist` at all.
- [`docs/self-managed/components/orchestration-cluster/core-settings/configuration/properties.md`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda-docs/blob/main/docs/self-managed/components/orchestration-cluster/core-settings/configuration/properties.md) — no occurrence of `tasklist`.
- Repository-wide search for `tasklisturl` and `tasklist-url`: the only matches are the Helm topology descriptor and the App Integrations / MS Teams pages, all unrelated to this property.

## Wider finding

While checking the above: the **Property reference** page composes its content from partials for `api`, `mcp`, `cluster`, `data`, `primary-storage`, `secondary-storage`, `exporters`, `expression`, `licensing`, `monitoring`, `process-instance-creation`, `processing`, `secrets`, `security` and `system`.

There is no `operate` partial, and no `tasklist` partial. The entire `camunda.operate.*` and `camunda.tasklist.*` property trees are therefore absent from the unified Property reference, even though the Orchestration Cluster ships them and `dist/src/main/config/defaults.yaml` in `camunda/camunda` generates a full reference for them.

So `tasklist-url` is the symptom I hit, but the gap is structural rather than a single missed row.

## Suggested change

1. Document `camunda.operate.tasklist-url` / `CAMUNDA_OPERATE_TASKLISTURL` on the Operate configuration page: what it controls (the Tasklist deep link in the Details tab), its `null` default, the effect of leaving it unset, and an example value for a unified Orchestration Cluster (`http://localhost:8080/tasklist`, or `https://<host>/<context-path>/tasklist`).
2. Consider whether the Property reference should carry `camunda.operate.*` and `camunda.tasklist.*` partials, so webapp properties are discoverable alongside the rest of the cluster configuration.

Point 1 stands on its own and is worth doing regardless of what happens with point 2 — or with the product-side fix proposed in [camunda/camunda#65161](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/issues/65161), since the property remains a valid override for split deployments either way.

## Affected versions

8.9, 8.10, and `next`. The property itself has existed far longer, so older versioned docs are missing it too.

items.title: Make every config field additive across extends
items.body:
## Problem

A config's `extends` chain merges by value kind. Maps (`routes`, `variants`) merge key by key, while lists (`rootDirs`, `exclude`) and strings are replaced by the child. This is not a deliberate rule per field. It falls out of the generic deep merge in `src/base/objects.ts`, which recurses into objects and overwrites everything else.

The docs state the principle as "a child can add or replace values but never remove them". Lists break it: a child that sets `exclude` or `rootDirs` silently drops every entry of its parent unless it copies them.

Concrete cases:

- A `prod.rogen.json` that adds `**/*.spec.luau` to `exclude` must restate every glob from `default.rogen.json`. When the parent gains a glob later, the child silently ships those files.
- Every place config restates `"src"` in `rootDirs`.
- A mode's `exclude` (#135) has to add to the config's, which the replace rule can't express.

## What other tools do

How a child's field combines with the same field in what it extends, per value kind:

| Tool | Scalar | Map | List | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tsconfig `extends` | child wins | `compilerOptions` merges by key | replaced (`include`, `exclude`, `files`, `lib`) | The replaced lists are the best-known complaint about `extends`; templates carry a comment telling users to copy the base entries |
| Babel `extends` / `env` | child wins | `assumptions`, `parserOpts`, `generatorOpts` merge by key | `plugins` and `presets` merge by item identity, replacing the matching entry | Lists are treated as keyed by what identifies an item |
| ESLint legacy `extends` | child wins | `rules` merge by key, a bare severity keeps inherited options | `extends`, `plugins`, `overrides` concatenate | Flat config dropped `extends` for an ordered array where the last match wins |
| Stylelint `extends` | child wins | `rules` merge by key | `plugins`, `extends`, `overrides` concatenate | |
| Docker Compose (`-f`, override file) | child wins | merged by key | **appended** | The one tool that documents all three rules in one place |
| Helm values (`-f`) | child wins | deep merge | replaced | Widely regarded as a footgun; the advice is "use maps instead of lists" |
| Kustomize strategic merge | child wins | merged | merged by a declared key, else replaced | Needs a schema to know the key |
| Netlify contexts | more specific wins | per property | per property | Override blocks, not inheritance |
| EAS `extends` between profiles | child wins | by key | n/a | |
| Gradle source sets | n/a | n/a | union | A variant's folders add to `main` |

Three findings:

1. **Scalars always take the child's value and maps always merge by key.** No tool disagrees. Rogen already does both.
2. **Lists are the only contested kind, and "replace" is the rule people complain about.** tsconfig and Helm replace, and both are cited as pain points. Compose, ESLint, Stylelint and Gradle append or union. Babel and Kustomize merge by identity, which is "append, and a repeated item replaces its earlier self".
3. **The tools that append all treat the list as a set of contributions, not a sequence to be re-stated.** That is what `exclude` and `rootDirs` are: every file in the chain contributes entries.

The one thing "replace" buys is removal. Every tool that appends gives removal a separate, explicit form (Kustomize `$patch: delete`, Compose `!reset`), or tells users to restructure the chain, which is what Rogen's docs already say.

## Decision

Make every field additive, with one rule: **a child adds to its parent and never removes.**

| Kind | Fields | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Map | `routes`, `variants`, `modes` | merged key by key; the child wins a key (unchanged) |
| List | `rootDirs`, `exclude` | the child's entries are appended to the parent's; a repeated entry keeps its last position |
| String | `template`, `syncDir`, `mode` | the child replaces (unchanged) |
| Not inherited | `outFile`, `$schema`, `extends` | unchanged |

A default applies only when no file in the chain sets the field. The CLI tier stays as it is.

This is the Compose rule, with Babel's identity merge for repeated entries. Keeping the last position of a repeated entry means every existing config keeps its meaning: `["src", "places/lobby"]` over a parent's `["src"]` still resolves to `src, places/lobby`, so "the later root dir wins" holds, and a child can still reorder by restating entries. There is no removal syntax; the documented way to drop a value stays "flip the chain".

The merge policy lives beside each field's schema, so a new field can't be added without saying how it merges.

## Behavior changes

- A child whose `exclude` deliberately left out one of its parent's globs now inherits it. The documented way to drop a value already is to flip the chain, so this only affects configs that relied on the undocumented replace.
- A parent that omits `rootDirs` to use the default `["src"]` no longer contributes `src` once a child sets `rootDirs`, because the default applies only when no file sets the field. `init` never writes this shape, and the missing-root warning covers the slip.

## Work

- [ ] Give each field in `config-schema.ts` a merge policy beside its schema, and merge layers by policy instead of the generic deep merge.
- [ ] Track the origin of every list entry, so a diagnostic about one `rootDirs` entry or `exclude` glob points at the file and position that wrote it (`LayeredConfig.locate`).
- [ ] `list --json` and `list` show the merged lists; check `extends` chain output still reads well.
- [ ] `init` writes a place's `rootDirs` as only the place folder (`["places/lobby"]`).
- [ ] Update the merge table and the "Extending Configs" section in the configuration docs, `help/config.md`, the multi-place guide and the schema descriptions. State the rule in one sentence and the removal story in the next.
- [ ] E2E cases: list append across a chain of three, dedupe keeping the last position, a diagnostic located in the parent's list, and the default-only-when-unset rule.

items.title: feat(auth): provision operator-managed accounts and tokens from config at startup
items.body:
## Problem

A twake deployment pulls its secrets from OpenBao. For the admin account this already works end to end: `ensure_admin_user` (`openrag/services/persistence/user_repo.py`) rewrites the `users.id = 1` token hash on every startup whenever `AUTH_TOKEN` is set, so rotating the value in OpenBao and restarting the pod is enough.

Every other account is still manual. `POST /users/` always generates a random `or-…` token and returns it once, so there is no way to make a user carry a token that was decided in OpenBao. In practice, for each service account (typically the one cozy-stack uses in its `rag:` config) and for each environment, an operator has to:

1. create the user through the API or SQL,
2. compute `sha256(<token from OpenBao>)` by hand,
3. `UPDATE users SET token = '<hash>' WHERE …`,
4. insert the partition memberships.

These steps are repeated on each fresh deployment and on each rotation, are easy to get wrong (hash of the wrong value, missing membership) and let OpenRag and its clients drift apart.

## Proposal

Generalise the admin bootstrap to a list of **operator-managed accounts**, declared in the config and provisioned at startup. The account's shape lives in the config (versioned), the secret stays in the environment (fed by OpenBao), and the app does the upsert.

```yaml
# conf/config.yaml
auth:
  seed_users:
    - external_user_id: svc-cozy-stack   # stable key, column is already unique
      display_name: cozy-stack
      token_env: COZY_STACK_TOKEN        # name of the env var, never the value
      is_admin: false
      partitions:
        - { name: twake, role: editor }
```

Semantics, mirrored on `ensure_admin_user` so behaviour stays predictable:

- **Env var set**: it is authoritative, the stored hash is rewritten. Rotation = change the value in OpenBao, restart the pod.
- **Env var unset**: the existing row is left untouched and a warning is logged. Startup does not fail, so OIDC deployments that do not define these accounts keep working.
- **Upsert only**: accounts and memberships are created or updated, never deleted. Lookup is by `external_user_id`, never by `id`.
- **Storage unchanged**: still SHA-256 in `users.token`, no migration.

Alternatives considered and why they are not the primary solution:

- *Accept a caller-supplied token on `POST /users/` plus a Helm post-upgrade Job calling the API*: removes the manual hashing but keeps one imperative step per deployment, and an API that accepts chosen tokens invites weak tokens. Could be a complement, not the main mechanism.
- *Store the hash in OpenBao and inject it with SQL*: recreates the manual step, just moved elsewhere.
- *Validate service tokens in memory without Postgres*: forks the auth logic, and memberships still live in the database anyway.

The real win: cozy-stack and OpenRag read the same OpenBao key, so the two sides cannot diverge.

## Implementation outline

1. `core/config/auth.py`: a `SeedUserConfig` Pydantic model and the `auth.seed_users` list.
2. `services/persistence/user_repo.py`: an `ensure_seed_users` method next to `ensure_admin_user` (upsert on `external_user_id`, then memberships).
3. `di/container.py`: a new `ServiceContainer.initialize` step. Memberships need the partitions to exist, and `seed_default_partition` currently runs *after* `ensure_admin_user`, so the ordering has to be adjusted (seed users after partitions, or create missing partitions on the fly).
4. Helm chart: nothing to change for the secrets flow. `vaultStaticSecret` / `externalSecret` with `dataFrom` already projects every key of the KV path as env vars. One addition: the Secret refreshes every 30 s but env vars need a pod restart, so add a Reloader annotation or a Secret checksum annotation on the Deployment.
5. Docs: `user_auth.md` and `env_vars.md`, with the cozy-stack example.
6. Unit tests on the repo method and on the config model.

## Out of scope

- Changing how `AUTH_TOKEN` / the admin account is handled.
- OIDC accounts (matched on `sub`, no token to seed).

items.title: Installing the chart is a research project, and a wrong values file renders a plausible install
items.body:
> Backlog entry 108, moved here from [`docs/backlog.md`](https://github.com/Flou21/hephaisto/blob/main/docs/backlog.md) (section *Chart and deployment*). The text below is the entry as it stood; that file is frozen.

**Symptom.** Deploying Hephaisto to its first real cluster took a day of reading the chart's own
source to answer questions the documentation does not, and produced **three separate mistakes in a
guide written by someone who had just read the whole repository**. A consumer has no such
advantage.

**The one that matters most: a values file can be entirely wrong and still render.** A Fleet bundle
whose `values.yaml` was still the placeholder from a different chart —

```yaml
controller:
  metrics:
    enabled: true
```

— renders with `exit=0`, no warning, and produces a **complete, plausible, all-defaults install**:
three `PrometheusRule` objects on a cluster that already has its own rules, a NetworkPolicy
admitting `hephaisto-obs` on a cluster whose Alertmanager is in `prometheus` (so no alert can ever
arrive, and the agent reports itself healthy — see #103's failure shape), a `PodMonitor`
labelled `release: kube-prometheus-stack`, and a Postgres host of `postgres.hephaisto` that does
not exist.

**Cause.** `values.schema.json` declares `required: [image, mode, observabilityNamespace,
prometheusOperator, policy, secrets, networkPolicy]`, which looks like it would catch this and
cannot: Helm validates the values **after** merging the chart's own defaults, so every `required`
key is always satisfied. And the root schema has no `additionalProperties: false`, so the
operator's stray keys are accepted in silence. The schema therefore validates the chart against
itself. It cannot fail.

**The other two mistakes, both from documentation that is wrong or absent rather than merely thin:**

1. **`grafanaMcp.url` needs the `/mcp` path and nothing says so where anyone would look.** The
   value is used verbatim as the streamable-http endpoint. `values.yaml` documents this key at
   length — what it costs to omit, how to find the datasource uids — and never shows a URL with a
   path. The only statement of the requirement is an XML doc comment on `GrafanaOptions.McpUrl`.
   Omit it and every tool is lost, which `values.yaml` itself warns is "much worse at diagnosis".

2. **`secrets.grafanaMcp` is described as something it usually is not.** `values.yaml` says *"The
   grafana-mcp bearer token: key `token`. Cannot exist before install - only Grafana can mint
   it"*, which reads unambiguously as a Grafana service-account token. On mcp-grafana ≥ 1.1.0 —
   which is what `--server-auth-token` exists for — there are **two** tokens: a caller bearer the
   MCP server validates (`MCP_GRAFANA_SERVER_TOKEN`), and grafana-mcp's own Grafana credential,
   which Hephaisto never sees. `secrets.grafanaMcp` is the **former**. This repo's own
   `scripts/bootstrap-secrets.sh` gets it right — it generates `grafana-mcp-caller-token` with
   `openssl rand -hex 32` and mints `grafana-mcp-grafana-token` separately — so the code and the
   script disagree with the chart comment, and the chart comment is the one an operator reads.

   The consequence is not a 401 that names itself. It is worse: guidance to scope that token
   "Viewer" to bound what `grafana_api_request` can do, which does nothing at all, because the
   scope that actually bounds it belongs to a token on the MCP server.

**Why none of this was caught.** Every install before this one was performed by this repository,
against a cluster this repository configured, from `values-dev.yaml` and
`scripts/bootstrap-secrets.sh`. Those two files encode all of the above correctly and neither is
what a consumer uses. It is #103's lesson one level up: the configuration that exposes the
defect is the one nobody here has, and v0.6.0 was the release that first invited a stranger to
have it.

**Fix.** Three parts, and the first is the cheap one.

- **Make a wrong values file fail.** `additionalProperties: false` on the root of
  `values.schema.json`, so a key the chart does not know is a `helm template` error rather than a
  silent default. Worth extending to the nested objects for the same reason.
- **Write a getting-started guide**, and have it answer the questions this deployment actually
  asked, in order: *I already run Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana — what do I turn off?* (the
  `alerts.*` group, which defaults **on** and therefore duplicates rules a real cluster already
  has); *how do I reach the console?* (port-forward, because the console shares port 8080 with the
  unauthenticated webhook and there is deliberately no Ingress); *what are the two Grafana tokens
  and which one goes where?*; *what does `observabilityNamespace` do if my Grafana and my
  Alertmanager are in different namespaces?* (it takes one value, and the answer is to forward
  Grafana's alerts to Alertmanager rather than to widen the policy); and a copy-pasteable set of
  `kubectl create secret` commands, which currently exist only as shell inside
  `bootstrap-secrets.sh` behind a dev-cluster context guard.
- **Correct the two comments above**, and add an example URL with `/mcp` to `values.yaml`.

**A fourth finding, from the same deployment: there is no safe way to expose the console.**

The console, the JSON API and `/webhooks/alertmanager` all answer on port **8080**, and the agent
has no authentication of its own — there is no `AddAuthentication` or `RequireAuthorization`
anywhere in `Hephaisto.Agent`. The NetworkPolicy is therefore the webhook's entire authentication,
and the chart is right to ship no Ingress template.

But an operator still has to look at the console, and "port-forward, forever" is not an answer for
a team. Every route out is a bad trade **because the two things share a port**:

| Route | What it costs |
|---|---|
| Ingress + identity proxy in front | The proxy must cover the whole host with no path exception, because `/webhooks` is on it |
| Ingress behind a `hostNetwork` controller | Needs an `ipBlock` for node addresses, because a hostNetwork pod carries the node's address and no `namespaceSelector` can match it. That hole also admits forged alerts from any hostNetwork pod on those nodes |
| A tunnel (cloudflared et al.) | Works cleanly — an ordinary pod, so `namespaceSelector` matches — but is a whole extra component to run |

The middle row was measured on 2026-09-11: with the chart's NetworkPolicy in place and
`ingress-nginx` running `hostNetwork: true` as a DaemonSet, the Ingress returned **504 Gateway
Timeout** — Calico drops rather than rejects, so the TCP connect hangs rather than failing fast,
and nothing in any log names the policy. It is the kubelet-probe trap in the chart's own
`extraIngressCIDRs` comment, one consumer over.

**Fix.** Separate the two concerns so the network layer is not asked to serve both:

- **Serve `/webhooks` on its own port** (a second Kestrel endpoint), so a NetworkPolicy can protect
  the webhook while the console is exposed by any ordinary means. This is the small change and it
  dissolves the whole table above.
- Or **authenticate the console and API**, which is the larger piece of work and is wanted anyway
  before `mode` is ever non-Observe — right now an identity proxy is the only thing in front of
  `POST /api/incidents/{id}/actions/{actionId}/approve`.

Either way the getting-started guide gains the section it currently cannot have.

**Not a nice-to-have.** v0.6.0's stated goal was *"Someone else can run it"*, and this is the first
evidence about whether that is true. Installing it is currently gated on reading the source — which
is a thing the AGPL guarantees you *may* do, not a thing a deployment should *require*.

**Size.** M for the install ergonomics; the schema change is S and should not wait for the guide.
The webhook port split is S and is the highest-leverage line in this entry.

**Three of the four parts shipped in v0.8.0.** `additionalProperties: false` on the schema root
and on the thirteen nested objects whose key set is closed - a values file belonging to another
chart is now a template error rather than a plausible all-defaults install, and locking it first
required declaring `grafana`, `grafanaMcp.datasourceUids` and `postgres.appUser`, which the schema
had never declared and nothing had ever compared. `/webhooks` on its own port, so
`networkPolicy.extraIngressCIDRs` now reaches the console and not the receiver - letting a node
address read a dashboard no longer lets it inject a forged alert. And both wrong comments
corrected: `secrets.grafanaMcp` is the caller bearer rather than a Grafana credential, and
`grafanaMcp.url` needs its `/mcp` path.

**The getting-started guide is what remains, and it carries with the rest of the
install-ergonomics work.** It was renumbered from v0.9.0 through v0.12.0. **High priority, after
[roadmap v0.12.0](https://github.com/Flou21/hephaisto/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md) (2026-09-29)**, when production problems took precedence. Writing one was deferred deliberately rather than forgotten: v0.8.0's
theme became operating the agent rather than installing it, on the grounds that installing is
something you do once and had just been done.

**Not planned for now, 2026-10-06.** The owner's decision: it comes later, other things come
first ([roadmap](https://github.com/Flou21/hephaisto/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md#not-planned-for-now)). The guide is still unwritten.

**Size of what is left.** M, and it is a writing job. Open, and not planned for now.

items.title: Support auto-unseal (KMS/HSM seals) in the self-managed OpenBao chart
items.body:
## Is this related to a problem? Please describe.
The bundled OpenBao chart (`deploy/helm/openbao`) only supports a single-share Shamir seal: the sidecar reads the unseal key from a Kubernetes Secret. There is no way to use an auto-unseal seal (a cloud KMS or an HSM), so the unseal key stays on the cluster.

## Describe the solution you'd like
An opt-in `server.autoUnseal` path that works with any OpenBao auto-unseal seal (`awskms`, `azurekeyvault`, `gcpckms`, `transit`, `pkcs11`): init with recovery keys instead of a Shamir key, skip the unseal Secret and sidecar, and ship an example overlay. Default stays Shamir.

Benefit: the seal unwraps the root key on start, so the unseal key is no longer a cluster Secret; seal use is governed by the provider's key policy.

## Describe alternatives you've considered
Tightening RBAC on the unseal Secret keeps the key on the cluster and adds nothing over an auto-unseal seal, since the sidecar already auto-unseals. An external managed Vault is a bigger change and not viable for per-cluster isolation.

## Additional context
A chart change is prepared: recovery-key init, the empty unseal Secret gated off, a seal-aware init script, and a provider-neutral example overlay (AWS KMS shown as the example). Storing or revoking the initial root token is unchanged and out of scope here.
