labels.description: Vetted by the factory; eligible for an agent to implement

items.body:
Part of #1615

PRD `docs/design/console/PRD-phase1-agents-workflows.md` AW-W1 (what starts it) and AW-W2 (enable toggle). Backend only; the card list and the reader switch are sibling issues.

**Today.** Which workflow starts how is hard-coded in four places: `select_workflow` in `services/daemon/plan_generator.py:190` (returns `incident-response`, `forensic-analysis`, `full-investigation`, falls back to `incident-response`), the scheduler's `"threat-hunt"` at `services/daemon/scheduler.py:244`, `SHADOW_WORKFLOW_ID` at `services/daemon/orchestrator.py:317`, and the two literals in `clients/web/src/shell/CommandBar.tsx:210-215`. Nothing on `GET /api/workflows` says any of it. There is no way to turn a workflow off except two env flags: `daemon_threat_hunt_enabled` and `orchestrator_shadow_adjudication` (`core/config.py:279,307`, `services/daemon/config.py:61,94`, `infra/docker/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/helm/vigil/values.yaml`).

**Build.**
- One module in `core/workflows/` (for example `routing.py`) holding `FALLBACK_WORKFLOW`, `ROUTED_WORKFLOWS`, `SCHEDULED_WORKFLOW`, `SHADOW_WORKFLOW_ID`. The daemon imports those names instead of its literals. A unit test proves `select_workflow` returns only members of `ROUTED_WORKFLOWS` over every branch.
- `catalog.listing` adds to each row `triggers` (a list drawn from `alerts`, `schedule`, `shadow`), `can_disable` (false only for `FALLBACK_WORKFLOW`), and `enabled`.
- Enablement, copying `core/agents/enablement.py` exactly: a `SystemConfig` row `workflows.disabled` holding `{"ids": [...]}`, written through `get_config_service(user_id=...)` so it is audited, one reader `disabled_workflow_ids()`, one setter, and a default-disabled set containing `shadow-adjudication`. Setting `enabled` on `FALLBACK_WORKFLOW` to false is refused with the reason.
- Route: `PUT /api/workflows/{workflow_id}/enabled` in `core/workflows/workflows_router.py`, same body and auth as `PUT /agents/{agent_id}/enabled` in `services/api/routers/agents.py:78`. 404 for an unknown id, 500 when the write returns False.
- Enforce where a run is chosen or started: `POST /workflows/{id}/execute` and the v1 start in `core/api/v1/agent_runs_router.py` refuse a disabled workflow with 409 and a detail naming it; the orchestrator's finding path (`orchestrator.py:777`) routes a disabled result to `FALLBACK_WORKFLOW` and logs that; `scheduler._run_threat_hunt` returns without queuing when `SCHEDULED_WORKFLOW` is disabled; `_enqueue_shadow_adjudication` returns when `SHADOW_WORKFLOW_ID` is disabled. Read the list at each call, as agents do; do not cache.
- Remove `daemon_threat_hunt_enabled` and `orchestrator_shadow_adjudication` everywhere they are read or set (core config, daemon config, compose, helm values). Keep `daemon_threat_hunt_interval`. Add a CHANGELOG line saying the switch is now in the console.
- `commandBar.ts`: the live commands that run a workflow carry its id; `CommandBar.tsx` `run()` reads it. The command bar surfaces the 409 the way it surfaces any failed command; do not add a second check.

**Do not build.** No per-workflow table or column, no migration, no frontmatter `triggers` key, no UI. `custom_workflows.is_active` stays the soft-delete.

**Tests** (`tests/unit/workflows/`): toggle round trip for a built-in and a custom id, with the audit row; the fallback refuses; execute and v1 start refuse a disabled id and accept an enabled one; routing falls back; the scheduler and shadow skip; `select_workflow` ratchet; listing carries `triggers`, `can_disable`, `enabled`; `shadow-adjudication` is off with no row.

**Verify live.** Start your own API on a free port. Turn `threat-hunt` off via the route, read it back on `GET /api/workflows`, start it with `/execute` and see the 409; turn it on and start it. Confirm `incident-response` refuses to turn off.

Done when the listing says what starts every workflow, a workflow can be turned off from the API and nothing starts it while it is off, and the two env flags are gone.

items.title: Super-charged tables: share views with everyone through the TableConfiguration CRD

labels.name: QA/dev-automation
labels.description: Issues that engineers have written automation around so QA doesn't have look at this

items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Saved table views (super-charged resource tables, https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/18745) are stored per user in user preferences, so a view can't be shared: an admin can't give everyone a "Needs attention" view on Pods, or choose the view a list opens on for all users. https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/57692 adds a `TableConfiguration` CRD (`tableconfigurations.ui.cattle.io`) for this; the UI needs to read and write it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The same saved view shape is used in two places:
- **Per user**: user preferences, as today. Only that user changes it.
- **Global**: `TableConfiguration` resources on the upstream cluster. Everyone with read access sees them; only users with the rights to create, update or delete them change them.

A resource is one of two types (full CRD below):
- **`PAGE`**: a page's configuration — its views (in tab order), its default view (`defaultViewId`) and where the table's own tab (All) sits (`allIndex`). The UI uses one per page (the oldest, if there are several).
- **`VIEW`**: one view, added to the page after the PAGE resource's views, oldest first. It has no position or default of its own.

`spec.page` says which list it applies to: the list's resource type (eg `pod`) or a page name (eg `home`).

Behaviour:
- **Tab strip**: shared views show as tabs marked with the groups icon before their name (tooltip "Published", as published views on a configurable page), after All and before the user's own, in one strip the user can reorder; the user's order of every tab is kept in their preferences (`order`).
- **Default view**: the user's own default wins and can be a shared view; without one, the PAGE resource's `defaultViewId` applies. Choosing All over a shared default is kept as `defaultViewId: all`.
- **Everyone**: duplicate a shared view, save changes to it as a new view of their own, export it, or make it their default.
- **Users who can create the resources**: "Publish" turns a view of their own into a `VIEW` resource under the same id (named `view-<page>-<id>`), keeping its place in the strip.
- **Users who can update / delete them**: save changes to, rename, "Unpublish" (back to a view of their own) or delete a shared view, with undo. A view inside a `PAGE` resource is edited in its `views` list.
- **Live**: changes to the resources show without a reload.
- **Without the CRD, or without read access to it**: the tables behave exactly as today.

The backend needs to give every user read access (get / list / watch) to `tableconfigurations`; without it a user sees no shared views. https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57751 installs the CRD at startup and adds that read access to the standard User global role.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- **Only `PAGE` resources**: one resource per page, but every share or edit rewrites the same list, so concurrent admin edits conflict, and other sources (extensions, Helm charts, GitOps) can't add a view without owning the page's resource.
- **Personal views in the CRD too**: Kubernetes RBAC can't limit editing a resource to its owner without a webhook, and it would mean a resource per user per page.

**Additional context**
To agree with the backend:
- **Per-user `order` and `defaultViewId`**: the user's preferences gain an `order` of every tab (shared ones included), and `defaultViewId` can be a shared view's id or `all`. These are additions to the per-user copy only; the CRD is unchanged.
- **`page` for the Cluster Management list**: the CRD's example is `provisioning.cattle.io.cluster`, but that list's table is built on `management.cattle.io.cluster`, which is what the UI uses today. `page` is a free string, so this is a convention to settle.
- **A `PAGE` with no views of its own** (eg only setting `defaultViewId` to a `VIEW` resource's view) must still have `views: []`; the CEL rule rejects it without the field.
- **Referencing `VIEW` resources from a `PAGE`**: the UI accepts a `VIEW` resource's view id as the `PAGE`'s `defaultViewId`, and when the same id is in both, keeps the `PAGE`'s copy. The CRD doesn't say either way.

Prototype: https://github.com/marcelofukumoto/dashboard/tree/proto-supercharged-tables-crd (built on https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/pull/19393).

The CRD itself: https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57751 (draft), as `ui.cattle.io/v1` in the existing `ui.cattle.io` version, with the schema above.

<details>
<summary>TableConfiguration CRD (as generated in https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57751)</summary>

```yaml
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  annotations:
    controller-gen.kubebuilder.io/version: v0.20.1
  name: tableconfigurations.ui.cattle.io
spec:
  group: ui.cattle.io
  names:
    kind: TableConfiguration
    listKind: TableConfigurationList
    plural: tableconfigurations
    shortNames:
    - tablecfg
    singular: tableconfiguration
  scope: Cluster
  versions:
  - additionalPrinterColumns:
    - jsonPath: .spec.type
      name: Type
      type: string
    - jsonPath: .spec.page
      name: Page
      type: string
    - jsonPath: .spec.view.name
      name: View
      type: string
    - jsonPath: .spec.views[*].name
      name: Views
      type: string
    - jsonPath: .spec.defaultViewId
      name: Default
      type: string
    - jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
      name: Age
      type: date
    name: v1
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        description: |-
          TableConfiguration is a configuration of the UI's resource tables shared with every user. Each user's own
          configuration is kept in their preferences; this is the one everyone starts from.
        properties:
          apiVersion:
            description: |-
              APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
              Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
              may reject unrecognized values.
              More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources
            type: string
          kind:
            description: |-
              Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
              Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
              Cannot be updated.
              In CamelCase.
              More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
            type: string
          metadata:
            type: object
          spec:
            description: Spec is the table configuration.
            properties:
              allIndex:
                description: AllIndex is where the table's own tab sits among the
                  saved ones. Missing means the front. Only for PAGE.
                minimum: 0
                type: integer
              defaultViewId:
                description: DefaultViewID is the id of the view selected when the
                  page opens. Only for PAGE.
                nullable: true
                type: string
              page:
                description: |-
                  Page is the location to apply customization. Could relate to a resource type (e.g.
                  provisioning.cattle.io.cluster) or a specific name like 'home'.
                minLength: 1
                type: string
                x-kubernetes-validations:
                - message: page is immutable
                  rule: self == oldSelf
              type:
                description: |-
                  Type is PAGE for page level configuration, and the UI will load only one of these per page. VIEW
                  contains a single table configuration, and the UI will supplement the page with these.
                enum:
                - PAGE
                - VIEW
                type: string
                x-kubernetes-validations:
                - message: type is immutable
                  rule: self == oldSelf
              view:
                description: View is a saved table configuration (SavedView). Only
                  for VIEW.
                properties:
                  columnOrder:
                    description: ColumnOrder are the column ids in order. Missing
                      or null means the table's own order.
                    items:
                      type: string
                    nullable: true
                    type: array
                  columns:
                    description: Columns are the column ids shown. Missing or null
                      means the table's default columns.
                    items:
                      type: string
                    nullable: true
                    type: array
                  groupBy:
                    description: GroupBy is the field id to group by, or 'none' to
                      turn off the table's default grouping.
                    nullable: true
                    type: string
                  id:
                    description: ID identifies the view, among a page's views and
                      in each user's preferences.
                    type: string
                  labelColumns:
                    description: LabelColumns are the label keys shown as columns.
                    items:
                      type: string
                    type: array
                  name:
                    description: Name is the view's name, shown on its tab.
                    type: string
                  query:
                    description: Query filters the table, as typed into its filter.
                    type: string
                  sort:
                    description: Sort is the column the table is sorted by. Missing
                      or null means the table's own sort.
                    nullable: true
                    type: string
                  sortDescending:
                    description: SortDescending sorts the table in descending order.
                    type: boolean
                required:
                - id
                - name
                type: object
              views:
                description: Views are the page's saved table configurations, in tab
                  order (SavedPage). Required for PAGE.
                items:
                  description: TableViewSaved is a saved table configuration.
                  properties:
                    columnOrder:
                      description: ColumnOrder are the column ids in order. Missing
                        or null means the table's own order.
                      items:
                        type: string
                      nullable: true
                      type: array
                    columns:
                      description: Columns are the column ids shown. Missing or null
                        means the table's default columns.
                      items:
                        type: string
                      nullable: true
                      type: array
                    groupBy:
                      description: GroupBy is the field id to group by, or 'none'
                        to turn off the table's default grouping.
                      nullable: true
                      type: string
                    id:
                      description: ID identifies the view, among a page's views and
                        in each user's preferences.
                      type: string
                    labelColumns:
                      description: LabelColumns are the label keys shown as columns.
                      items:
                        type: string
                      type: array
                    name:
                      description: Name is the view's name, shown on its tab.
                      type: string
                    query:
                      description: Query filters the table, as typed into its filter.
                      type: string
                    sort:
                      description: Sort is the column the table is sorted by. Missing
                        or null means the table's own sort.
                      nullable: true
                      type: string
                    sortDescending:
                      description: SortDescending sorts the table in descending order.
                      type: boolean
                  required:
                  - id
                  - name
                  type: object
                type: array
                x-kubernetes-list-map-keys:
                - id
                x-kubernetes-list-type: map
            required:
            - page
            - type
            type: object
            x-kubernetes-validations:
            - message: views is required when type is PAGE and not allowed when type
                is VIEW
              rule: 'self.type == ''PAGE'' ? has(self.views) : !has(self.views)'
            - message: view is required when type is VIEW and not allowed when type
                is PAGE
              rule: 'self.type == ''VIEW'' ? has(self.view) : !has(self.view)'
            - message: defaultViewId and allIndex are only allowed when type is PAGE
              rule: self.type == 'PAGE' || (!has(self.defaultViewId) && !has(self.allIndex))
        required:
        - spec
        type: object
    served: true
    storage: true
    subresources: {}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Examples</summary>

```yaml
# The Pods list's page configuration: one view of its own, which it opens on
apiVersion: ui.cattle.io/v1
kind: TableConfiguration
metadata:
  name: page-pod
spec:
  type: PAGE
  page: pod
  views:
    - id: gpodrunning
      name: Running (all teams)
      query: "state:running"
  defaultViewId: gpodrunning
  allIndex: 0
---
# One more view on the Pods list
apiVersion: ui.cattle.io/v1
kind: TableConfiguration
metadata:
  name: view-pod-gkubesystem
spec:
  type: VIEW
  page: pod
  view:
    id: gkubesystem
    name: Kube System (team)
    query: "namespace:kube-system"
    groupBy: "none"
---
# A view on the Home page's cluster list
apiVersion: ui.cattle.io/v1
kind: TableConfiguration
metadata:
  name: view-home-ghomeactive
spec:
  type: VIEW
  page: home
  view:
    id: ghomeactive
    name: Active (team)
    query: "state:active"
```

items.title: Remove the server and the Helm chart from agntcy/oasf
items.body:
Do this once chart v2 is released and in use, so there is always a working way to ship a server fix.

## Tasks
- Delete `server/`, `install/`, `docker-bake.hcl`, `.trivyignore`, and the server-only workflows and CI jobs.
- Keep the schema and proto tests. Add a CI job that loads the PR's schema with the pinned `oasf-server` version (integrity tests plus an endpoint smoke test).
- Add `task server:up` and `task server:reload`, which run the pinned server image with the local `schema/` mounted, so schema authors can preview their changes.
- Rewrite `RELEASE.md` (D9):
  - schema tags only, with no server steps,
  - release branches take schema-content fixes only.
- Update `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODEOWNERS` and the compatibility matrix in `proto/README.md` to point to `agntcy/oasf-server`.
- Remove `agntcy/oasf`'s write access to the `oasf-server` GHCR package.

## Acceptance criteria
- `agntcy/oasf` contains only schema, proto and docs.
- A schema PR that the server can't load fails CI.

items.title: k8s lexicon: project-local CRDs, typed Helm values, render patching, YAML include, typed composite overrides
items.body:
Feature gaps in the k8s lexicon (and its Helm render path), found in a survey of what a typed Kubernetes authoring tool should cover.

- [x] **1. Project-local CRD types.**
  A CRD gets typed classes only when it is listed in the lexicon's `CRD_SOURCES` (`lexicons/k8s/src/crd/crd-sources.ts`) and the lexicon is regenerated. Anyone using an operator the lexicon doesn't ship falls back to `k8sManifest`: no typed constructor, no lint-time spec validation, no LSP hover.
  Proposal: let a project declare its own CRD sources (local file, pinned URL, multi-document bundle), for example a `k8s.crds` key in `chant.config.ts` with an optional output directory. The build generates typed classes into the project with the existing CRD parser. Generation stays deterministic and refuses unpinned sources, as `CRD_SOURCES` already does.

- [x] **2. Typed values for third-party Helm charts.**
  `HelmRender` takes `values` as `Record<string, unknown>`, so a misspelled or wrongly shaped value is caught when `helm template` runs, or not at all if the chart ignores unknown keys.
  Proposal: when a chart publishes `values.schema.json`, generate a TypeScript values type from it and type `HelmRender`'s `values` with it, for repository charts and local chart paths. The converter must handle `$defs` references, keys with slashes or non-camelCase names, and objects nested inside `additionalProperties` maps.

- [x] **3. Patching rendered output.**
  Resources from a Helm render or a kustomize build root are finished documents with no way to adjust them in chant. If a chart doesn't expose a field, the options are forking the chart or an overlay outside chant.
  Proposal: a typed patch hook on rendered entities. Select documents by kind, name and namespace, then apply a JSON Patch or deep merge before serialization. Patched documents keep ownership stamping and post-synth checks, and `lifecycle diff --live` treats the patched form as the declared state.

- [x] **4. Including plain YAML.**
  There is no direct way to bring in a single manifest file or pinned URL as-is. The workaround is a kustomization directory that only lists the file or URL as a resource.
  Proposal: a declarable that loads a local or pinned remote multi-document YAML at build time. Its documents become entities like kustomize-root output, and the patch hook from (3) can target them.

- [x] **5. Typed passthrough on composites.**
  Composites such as `StatefulApp` and `WebApp` take `defaults` overrides typed as `Partial<Record<string, unknown>>`, so setting gRPC probes, probe HTTP headers, `enableServiceLinks`, `revisionHistoryLimit` or extra `volumeClaimTemplates` through a composite has no type checking.
  Proposal: type each member's `defaults` against that member's generated props.

- [x] **6. Correct the Kubernetes version pin.**
  `PINNED_VERSIONS.k8sOpenAPI` in `lexicons/k8s/src/codegen/versions.ts` reads `v1.32.0`, but the generated types already include 1.34 APIs (`resource.k8s.io/v1`, `PodCertificateRequest`, `fileKeyRef`, `hostnameOverride`). Make the pin match what codegen uses.
